original_question: For a group Γ that is not residually soluble, determine structural properties of the true prosoluble kernel Ker(Γ -> PS(Γ)) = intersection_{n>=0} D^n(Γ), where D^n(Γ) denotes the derived series terms. In particular, develop descriptions or invariants for this kernel in concrete families such as non-residually-soluble one-relator groups, wreath products of the type discussed in the paper, amalgamated free products of nilpotent groups over cyclic subgroups, parafree groups, and free-by-free groups that are not residually soluble.
target_in_paper: Introduction, item (ii), as made explicit in §6.F: for a group that is not residually soluble, determine properties of the true prosoluble kernel Ker(Γ→PS(Γ)); §6.F identifies this kernel with the intersection of the derived series and then lists concrete classes of examples to investigate. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper: it correctly focuses on the true prosoluble kernel of a non-residually-soluble group, uses the right kernel formula Ker(Γ→PS(Γ))=⋂_{n≥0}D^n(Γ), and names most of the example families singled out in §6.F. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s formulation should state what PS(Γ) is: the true prosoluble completion attached to the family S of all normal subgroups N◁Γ such that Γ/N is soluble. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

The notation D^n(Γ) should be fixed explicitly as the ordinary derived series of the abstract group, with D^0(Γ)=Γ and D^{n+1}(Γ)=[D^n(Γ),D^n(Γ)]; the identification of the kernel with ⋂_{n≥0}D^n(Γ) uses the fact that S and (D^n(Γ))_{n≥0} define the same procompletion. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

The official wording is open-ended—“find out properties” of the kernel—rather than a request for a full classification or a new package of invariants; your draft is slightly broader/stronger than the paper’s own formulation. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

The nearby context includes a benchmark example that should be built into a stand-alone formulation: Γ=⟨a,b | a=[a,a^b]⟩, for which Baumslag’s result implies that the profinite kernel is D(Γ), that D(Γ) is perfect, hence that the true prosoluble kernel is also D(Γ), and that Γ/D(Γ)≅ℤ. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

The paper’s exact list of families is: other non-residually-soluble one-relator groups; wreath products as in §6.B; free products of nilpotent groups with amalgamation; parafree groups; and meta-residually soluble groups, with free-by-free groups singled out as a particular case. Your draft omits the umbrella class “meta-residually soluble groups” and narrows “free products of nilpotent groups with amalgamation” to cyclic amalgamation, which is not how §6.F itself states it. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

If parafree groups are kept in the question, their meaning is implicit from the paper’s cross-reference to §7.B: a parafree group is residually nilpotent and has the same lower-central quotients as a free group. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or “for sufficiently large m” quantifier is part of this problem; the missing stand-alone details are purely group-theoretic. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
refined_question: For an abstract group Γ that is not residually soluble, what can be said about the true prosoluble kernel Ker(φ_S:Γ→PS(Γ)), where PS(Γ) is the completion of Γ with respect to all normal subgroups N◁Γ for which Γ/N is soluble? Equivalently, by §5.D, determine D^∞(Γ)=⋂_{n≥0}D^n(Γ), where D^0(Γ)=Γ and D^{n+1}(Γ)=[D^n(Γ),D^n(Γ)]. As a benchmark, recover the Baumslag one-relator example Γ=⟨a,b | a=[a,a^b]⟩, for which Ker(φ_S)=D(Γ), D(Γ) is perfect, and Γ/D(Γ)≅ℤ; and investigate the same kernel for the examples explicitly listed in §6.F: other non-residually-soluble one-relator groups, wreath products Γ=S wr T as in §6.B with S soluble non-abelian and T soluble infinite, free products of nilpotent groups with amalgamation, parafree groups, and meta-residually soluble groups, in particular free-by-free groups that are not residually soluble. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, determine the intersection of all normal subgroups N◁Γ such that Γ/N is soluble, since §5.D shows that this is the same kernel as D^∞(Γ)=⋂_{n≥0}D^n(Γ). ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest paper-faithful target because the introduction explicitly singles out kernel questions arising from non-residual-solubility and says that an example is worked out in §6.F, while §6.F states the open problem itself and supplies the sample one-relator calculation plus the precise list of example families. Sections 5.B and 5.D provide the hidden notation needed to make the question stand alone: the derived-series conventions and the equivalence between the soluble-quotient family S and the countable family (D^n(Γ))_{n≥0}. The draft is therefore substantially correct, but it should be tightened by adding the definition of PS(Γ), the derived-series conventions, the benchmark Baumslag example, and the exact family list/wording used by the paper. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
